2026–2027 EER approved 9 June 2026. Articles 1.1, 3.2–3.7, 5.2–5.3 and 5.8–5.9, plus Appendix 3, control the cohort, curriculum, progression, thesis and internship.

curriculum: The 2026–2027 regulations confirm the English, full-time Maastricht BSc, 180 EC over three years. Article 3.6 and Appendix 3 give Year 1 as 41 EC of courses and 19 EC of longitudinal development, lab and design work. Year 2 is 38 EC of courses and 22 EC in the longitudinal lines, including one 7 EC design project. The first-listed Clinical Track is a neutral example and the Technological Track is an alternative. The 5 EC lab work and 2 EC attendance units appear once per year. Year 3 has a 30 EC minor followed by one 30 EC individual graduation project, including internship, thesis and oral defence. The internship and defence codes are components of that award. The minor remains open, with approval required where applicable. No mandatory named minor or additional project credit is inferred.
progression: Article 5.3 gives unconditional progression after all 60 Year 1 credits and after the full 120 first- and second-year credits. Conditional Year 2 entry requires three of four eight-week courses, one of two four-week courses and two of three longitudinal lines with the specified lab-credit condition. Conditional Year 3 entry also requires all Year 1 credits and corresponding Year 2 course and longitudinal-line minima. The standard example completes each year before entering the next. Article 3.7 allows an approved set of electives to supplement a shorter minor to 30 EC and sets conditions for external choices. Articles 5.2, 5.8 and 5.9 set the 6.0 minimum for the internship/thesis/defence, individual writing and oral assessment by two examiners, and a supervised placement meeting programme rules.

Compulsory; year 1, period 2; mathematics, physics, mechanics of materials, rheology, thermodynamics, circuits, CAD and finite-element modelling
Compulsory; year 1, period 3; scope, history, ethics and applications of regenerative medicine
Compulsory; year 1, period 4; anatomy, physiology and immunology
Compulsory; year 1, period 5; scripting in R, statistics and data analysis
The Intrinsic Regenerative Capacity of the Human Body (RMT1006)
Compulsory; year 1, period 6; wound healing, regeneration versus repair, ageing and the limits of regeneration
Compulsory longitudinal line; learning skills, professional behaviour, scientific storytelling and personal development
Compulsory longitudinal line; laboratory skills aligned with the first-year courses
Compulsory; attendance component of the year-1 lab skills line
Compulsory longitudinal line; expert interviews, site visits, journal clubs and a project pitch
Compulsory; year 2, period 1; stem-cell sources, potency, cell manufacture and cell-biomaterial constructs
Compulsory; year 2, period 2; design, synthesis and characterisation of biomaterials and cell-material interaction
Compulsory; year 2, period 3; cell therapy, immunotherapy, gene therapy, biomaterials, implants and medical devices
Compulsory; year 2, period 4; multivariable calculus, differential-equation and data-driven modelling, introduction to neural networks
Compulsory; year 2, period 5; micro- and nanofabrication, microfluidics, organs-on-chips and biofabrication
Both explore how ideas become marketable products. Maastricht focuses on the value of regenerative-medicine research. UCR teaches general venture design and validation.
Compulsory longitudinal line; includes choosing electives, minor and thesis subject
Compulsory longitudinal line; laboratory skills aligned with the second-year courses
Compulsory; attendance component of the year-2 lab skills line
Selected track of the year-2 design project line (the alternative is the Technological Track, RMT2104, 7 EC)
Students complete a 30 EC minor. Choices can include courses at Maastricht or another university, with approval where required.
Bachelor thesis with internship and presentation/defence (RMT3010, RMT3011, RMT3012)
Maastricht’s 30 EC graduation project combines an internship, an individual thesis and an oral defence. UCR’s optional independent research is outside the scheduled plan.
